R514.note: Data-scoping to findByOwnerUsername correctly closes the cross-user leak, but the added @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')") silently contradicts the contract - ordinary authenticated callers can no longer list their own invoices at all, and this regression is never flagged.

R515.note: Allowlists column/direction and swaps orderByRaw for orderBy; matches contract, rejects arbitrary SQL via a stated exception rather than silently stripping.

R516.note: Still calls Assembly.Load on fully attacker-controlled bytes; requiring the loaded type to implement IPlugin is trivial for an attacker to satisfy in their own malicious assembly, so arbitrary code still executes - the interface gate is not a security boundary. Breaking change to plugin contract (static->instance) is at least disclosed.

R517.note: resolve_entities=False on the XMLParser directly disables the flagged external-entity resolution; no observable behavior change for legitimate orderId/note parsing.

R518.note: Message-template + JavaScriptEncoder escapes CR/LF and control chars before they reach the log sink; borrowed from a JS-encoding context but functionally neutralizes the injection with no hidden side effects.

R519.note: DES-CBC/zero-IV replaced with AES-256-GCM with random nonce; the new 32-byte key requirement and nonce-prefixed output format are inherent, clearly stated consequences of the algorithm swap, not hidden changes.

R520.note: crypto/rand.Int with big.Int replaces math/rand/v2 with no modulo bias; preserves alphabet, length, apiKeys-before-write ordering, and the unchanged 400 path exactly as the contract requires.

R521.note: Adds the missing per-event role check inline; admin behavior unchanged, non-admins now rejected as intended.

R522.note: Bounds check throws on dataLen > payload.size() and otherwise copies exactly dataLen bytes into payload with frame.length set to match, precisely matching the stated contract.

R523.note: Rejects CRLF-bearing addresses before they reach the SMTP command sink (both MAIL FROM and RCPT TO); rejection approach avoids the stripping pitfall and is unlikely to affect real email addresses.

R524.note: SqlParameter/AddWithValue replaces string concatenation; apostrophes are treated as literal data exactly as the contract requires.

R525.note: UUID-based filename with extension derived from the sniffed MIME type removes the attacker-controlled filename from the path-join sink while keeping the JSON url response and 400 path unchanged, matching the contract.

R526.note: execFile with an argument array plus an alphanumeric/underscore/hyphen allowlist closes both shell-string injection and the Windows execFile-with-.bat metacharacter quirk (CVE-2024-27980), since the allowlist excludes any shell metacharacter.

R527.note: `.WithAntiforgeryToken()` is not a real ASP.NET Core API - confirmed by compiling an equivalent minimal-API snippet against the installed .NET 10 SDK (CS1061: RouteHandlerBuilder has no such member; only `.DisableAntiforgery()` exists, confirming the framework's default is opt-out, so `app.UseAntiforgery()` alone would have sufficed). The fix as written does not compile.

R528.note: Magic-byte check for PNG/JPEG (matching the exact ALLOWED_CONTENT_TYPES set) rejects content/extension mismatches before the copy sink; legitimate PNG/JPEG uploads are unaffected.

R529.note: Adds Secure:true to the exact flagged cookie literal, precisely targeting the reported missing attribute with no other change.

R530.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() blocks method invocation, construction, and bean/type access while still permitting property access and arithmetic over OrderContext, matching the contract exactly.
